title: The land and its conditions
summary: The land is described as consecrated, with conditional promises concerning liberty, captivity, iniquity, and righteousness. The passage also says the land should be kept from the knowledge of other nations, which would overrun it and leave no place for an inheritance.

explicit_facts.text: The land is consecrated unto him whom he shall bring.

If they serve him according to his commandments, the land shall be a land of liberty unto them, and they shall not be brought down into captivity; if they are brought into captivity, it shall be because of iniquity.
If iniquity abounds, the land shall be cursed for their sakes; unto the righteous it shall be blessed forever.
The land should be kept as yet from the knowledge of other nations, because many nations would overrun it, leaving no place for an inheritance.
